content: NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution must never be injected into the eye, including the anterior chamber or subconjunctival space. Topical antibiotics, particularly neomycin sulfate, can cause skin sensitization. The exact frequency of hypersensitivity reactions, such as skin rashes, is not well established. Sensitization to topical antibiotics often presents as itching, redness, and swelling of the conjunctiva and eyelid. In some cases, sensitization may appear as a failure of the condition to improve. Patients using topical antibiotics for extended periods should be monitored for these signs, and the medication should be discontinued if such symptoms occur. Symptoms typically resolve quickly after stopping the medication. Patients who develop sensitization should avoid using products containing these ingredients in the future. Prolonged use of NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution may lead to the overgrowth of organisms that are not susceptible to the medication, including fungi. Bacterial resistance to NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution may also occur. If symptoms such as purulent discharge, inflammation, or pain worsen, the patient should stop using the medication and consult a physician. There have been cases of bacterial keratitis associated with the use of multi-dose ophthalmic products that were inadvertently contaminated, often in patients with pre-existing corneal disease or damage to the ocular epithelial surface. Patients may experience allergic cross-reactions that could prevent the future use of antibiotics such as kanamycin, paromomycin, streptomycin, and possibly gentamicin. Patients should be instructed to avoid touching the tip of the dispensing container to the eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination. Sharing the product with others may spread infections. Improper handling of ocular products can lead to contamination with bacteria that cause eye infections, potentially resulting in severe eye damage and vision loss. If symptoms persist, worsen, or if an allergic reaction such as a rash occurs, patients should stop using the product and consult a physician. Patients should not use this product if they are allergic to any of its ingredients. The container should be kept tightly closed when not in use and stored out of reach of children. Long-term studies to assess the carcinogenic or mutagenic potential of polymyxin B sulfate or gramicidin have not been conducted in animals. In vitro studies with neomycin have shown an increase in chromosome aberrations at high concentrations (80 µg/mL), but the relevance of these findings to humans is unknown. The effects of neomycin on human carcinogenesis and mutagenesis remain unclear. Polymyxin B has been reported to impair equine sperm motility, but its effects on human male or female fertility are not known. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B sulfate, or gramicidin. It is not known whether this medication can harm a fetus or affect reproductive capacity when administered to a pregnant woman. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in breast milk, caution should be exercised when administering NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution to nursing mothers. The safety and effectiveness of NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution in pediatric patients have not been established. Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 and older to determine whether their response differs from that of younger patients. However, other clinical experience has not identified significant differences in responses between elderly and younger patients.
